summary: Backend-only verification of fingerprint-based extension version gate + /buy bot command. Targeted 48 tests across the 9 files listed in the review ALL PASS (48/48). External curl verification of new middleware behavior passes: X-Fingerprint present + no version header => 426 (new behavior), X-Fingerprint + old version => 426, X-Fingerprint + current 2.3.5 => 401 (auth, not 426), no fingerprint (curl/dashboard) => 401 (no 426), exempt paths /api/health and /api/public/version => 200 even with X-Fingerprint. However, running the FULL test suite shows 79 pre-existing test files broken by the middleware tightening (they send X-Fingerprint without X-Extension-Version and now correctly get 426 where they previously expected 400/401/403/200). These are not regressions to the targeted feature but they are regressions to the broader test suite that the main agent must update.

minor.issue: 79 pre-existing tests in 9 other test files (test_bins_phase_b, test_charge_only_persistence, test_db_nuke, test_extension_releases, test_fake_charge_edge_cases, test_formatters, test_hit_pipeline, test_iteration5_bug_fixes, test_public_mute in cross-file order) send X-Fingerprint without X-Extension-Version and now hit 426. These tests need X-Extension-Version=2.3.5 added to their headers (or the fixture in conftest.py needs to inject it globally when X-Fingerprint is set). The 48 targeted tests were updated but these were not.

action_items: Update the 9 non-targeted test files (or add global fixture) to include X-Extension-Version=2.3.5 alongside X-Fingerprint. Suggested one-line fix: in tests/conftest.py, whenever a test client fixture injects X-Fingerprint, also inject X-Extension-Version. This will restore all 79 failing tests without changing production code.
critical_code_review_comments: The middleware behavior is correct and matches the spec; the regression is only in older test fixtures that pre-date the fingerprint-based gate.
Consider centralizing extension-request header injection in conftest to avoid this class of drift in the future.

success_rate.backend: 100% on the 48 targeted tests; 55% (97/176) on the full suite due to un-updated legacy test files

context_for_next_testing_agent: The core feature (fingerprint-based version gate + /buy bot command) is working correctly, verified by 48/48 targeted tests + external curl. The 79 full-suite failures are all shape `assert 426 == <expected>` because those test files send X-Fingerprint without X-Extension-Version. Fix in one place: patch conftest to inject X-Extension-Version alongside X-Fingerprint, or update each test file's headers. Once done, re-run full pytest to confirm zero regressions.
rca of the issue: New middleware treats X-Fingerprint as the extension-detection signal. Any request with X-Fingerprint but no (or old) X-Extension-Version is now rejected with 426. This intentional change breaks 79 legacy tests that had been sending X-Fingerprint without a version header, expecting the old lenient behavior.
